title: Context Budgeting Playbook (scratch)
content:
Quick brain-dump: idea to automatically allocate a per-request "context budget" that trades off left-context retention, prefix caching use, and truncation/pinning strategies to meet token-cost and latency SLOs for different customer tiers.

Problem we see: customers have bursty conversational workloads where long histories drive cost and degrade latency. Current knobs (max_length, manual truncation rules, per-route config) are crude and require ops knowledge. We can make a smarter, automated layer that: 1) understands which tokens in context matter for quality, 2) enforces a soft budget aligned to cost/latency targets, and 3) falls back gracefully (pin key system prompts, drop less-important messages).

High level goal: reduce per-conversation token spend by 15-40% for median workloads while keeping subjective quality degradation < 5% on eval prompts. Provide configurable controls at route and tenant level (hard budget, soft budget with degradation profile).

Who benefits: product teams building chat assistants, conversational customer support, copilots that keep long histories. Also useful for Dedicated and Private customers who want predictable token costs.

Core concepts / primitives:
- Context budget: X tokens per call (or per session turn) enforced by a context manager. Can be absolute (tokens) or cost-weighted.
- Importance scoring: fast heuristic model (tiny transformer or TF-IDF+recency) that assigns importance to parts of the history (system prompts, last N messages, highlighted messages). Scores used for dropping/truncation priority.
- Pinning: user/system messages or entities the app marks as not-evictable (e.g., safety prompt, customer profile blob).
- Compression: cheap compression transforms (sentence-level summarization, keyword extraction, convo-slices) applied when budget exceeded.
- Progressive degradation policy: soft budget triggers staged actions (1: compact less-recent messages, 2: drop low-importance messages, 3: compress remaining, 4: if still over budget, truncate oldest non-pinned).

User stories (rough):
- PM: "As a PM, I want to set a token budget per API route so my app's monthly spend stays predictable."
- SRE: "As SRE, I want an automatic mode that keeps p95 latency under 400ms by reducing context when under load."
- Developer: "As a developer, I want to mark messages as pinned and indicate that profile context must never be compressed."
- Customer success: "As CS, I want to provide a recommended budget template for support bots with heavy transcript retention."

Metrics to measure success:
- Delta in tokens per call (median and p90)
- Quality regression on a curated eval set (ROUGE / embedding-sim vs full-context baseline + human spot checks)
- Latency impact (p50/p95 per route)
- Percent of calls where progressive degradation had to do aggressive truncation
- Customer feedback / support tickets related to lost context or hallucination increases

Design notes / implementation ideas:
- Opt-in per-route or per-tenant with a safe default (disabled).
- Implement as middleware in Redwood serving runtime so it can hook into batching and cache layers. Budget decision must run fast (sub-ms heuristics) and produce a compacted context for the actual model call.
- Importance scoring: offload to a microservice that caches scores for recent messages; use simple recency+role+embedding-similarity-to-last-turn as fallback if model scoring not available. Keep model-based scoring as an opt-in premium feature.
- Compression pathways: prefix summarization (summarize contiguous older messages into 1-2 bullets), entity-only keepers (pull named entities and key facts), and token-level lossy compression (byte-pair style) is too risky. Prefer semantic summarization + key-value profile extraction.
- SDK/metadata: allow SDK to mark pins and suggest message importance via headers (x-rw-pin: true, x-rw-importance: 0.8). Also expose API to query estimated token cost pre-call and post-call actuals.
- Integration with caching: if a prefix is cacheable and already stored, budget layer should consume zero budget for cached prefix and only count new tokens. Need to integrate with Redwood prefix cache indexes.

Edge cases / risks:
- Over-compression causing hallucinations or data loss (safety and correctness risk). Must run evals with domain-specific prompts (support transcripts, legal, medical).
- Latency: scoring + compression adds CPU; must be bounded and optionally run asynchronously with speculative generation? Could precompute importance/summaries per-session in background.
- Customer confusion: need clear telemetry and ways to disable auto-budget per-tenant. Policy transparency required (show which messages were compressed/dropped).

Experiment plan (MVP):
- Phase 0: offline eval harness. Implement importance heuristics and basic summarizer. Simulate budgets on historical transcripts, compute token savings and quality delta.
- Phase 1: opt-in beta on hosted API for small number of routes. Minimal runtime: recency heuristic + prefer last N messages + simple summarizer for >budget. Telemetry dashboard showing dropped/compressed tokens.
- Phase 2: add SDK pins + per-tenant configs + integration with prefix cache accounting. Expand to Dedicated with config flags.
- Phase 3: model-backed importance scoring, adaptive budgets by SLA/cost, and UI controls in Redwood Console (per-route budget slider + traces).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who owns safety/regression tests for compressed contexts? Ask Applied ML + Eval team.
- How to represent compression provenance in audit logs for Private customers? Add metadata with redacted diffs? Security review needed.
- Pricing implications: if budgets reduce token usage, do we recommend customers reduce commitments? Need pricing + finance input.
- UX: how to surface to developers what changed (diff viewer for compressed context).

Next steps (short):
- Sync with Arjun (SRE) to estimate runtime CPU cost & feasibility in serving runtime (this week).
- Grab dataset of 10k anonymized convo transcripts from support bots for offline sim (ask CS for export).
- Draft a one-pager for product leadership with expected impact and ask for a small infra sandbox allocation.

Notes to self: keep this as a loose playbook. Focus MVP on heuristics that are cheap and reversible. Avoid black-box summarizers for legal/regulated customers. Consider adding a mode that only triggers under latency pressure (reactive) vs always-on cost-saver (proactive).

References / inspiration: conversation trimming literature, RAG chunking heuristics, RLHF papers about context sensitivity (notes), and existing Redwood features: prefix cache, rollout policies, and per-route telemetry.

End of scratch notes.
